== Biography ==
{{African-American Sticker}}
Patrick was born in 1830 in Pennsylvania. He was the son of [[Brom-40|Mary Brom]] and [[Glasgow-752|Robert Glasgow]]. 

He lost his younger brother during the Civil War.  [[Glasgow-751|London Glasgow]] was a member of the 54th Massachusetts Volunteer Infantry, the first regiment in the United States made up entirely of enlisted men of color.  Patrick was also registered for the draft, but does not appear to have served. <ref>[[#military|Consolidated Civil War Draft Registrations]]</ref>

===Occupations===
* 1860: Farmhand
* 1850: Laborer

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-752]] is assessed at 91% (proved). Patrick’s 1830 Pennsylvania birth and 1850/1860 West Marlborough family citations fit Robert’s child group. Amy’s later explicit daughter relationship and the sustained sibling account strengthen Robert as father, while Patrick’s own early censuses do not name relationships.

Held citation and associated historical narrative address this selected father-child identity; no original was newly inspected.

Next useful test: Read Patrick’s death or a Robert probate entry naming him.
